name: axis-03-white-nosupport
version_tag: MECHANICAL CALENDAR AXIS — white plate RESLICED WITH SUPPORTS OFF. axis-01 ran with enable_support 1 and support_on_build_plate_only 0, which let the slicer climb the model and pack EVERY THREAD VALLEY: 2484 support moves inside the two nut bores and 9974 within 6mm of the bolt axis spanning z44.4-96.6, exactly the upper thread. That is both the support Ron should not have had to remove AND the reason the threads appeared absent — they were buried, not missing. THE THREADS ARE FINE AND THEY MATE: bolt upper thread minor dia 8.6 / major 11.0, nut bore minor 9.6 / major 12.0, i.e. 0.5mm radial clearance, a workable printed fit. Separating real overhang from thread flank on the bolt: only TWO near-horizontal ledges exist, 156.7mm2 at z23.00 and 170.4mm2 at z28.30 (the flange), totalling 327mm2. The other ~1596mm2 the slicer saw is thread flank, 1-9mm2 per layer, which must never be supported. No threshold-angle tweak separates those cleanly because thread flanks here really are near-horizontal, and build-plate-only support would still tower up alongside the shaft. So supports come off entirely and the two flange ledges print as unsupported 3mm annular overhangs — expect slight droop on their undersides, which are seating faces, not cosmetic. BRIM 8mm STAYS: bolt is 97mm tall on 380mm2 (ratio 4) and the washer is chamfered both faces, resting on 0.6mm2 with its real 171.8mm2 face floating at z=0.59.
